items.title: Mississauga and Brampton Hospitals Among 26 Sites Getting $47M Push to Cut ER Wait Times
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Ontario government announced Wednesday it will spend more than $47 million over four years on a new Emergency Department Action Team, or EDAT, that will work directly with 26 hospitals across the province to cut emergency room wait times. Insauga reports Mississauga and Brampton hospitals are among the sites included, specifically William Osler Health System's Brampton Civic Hospital and Etobicoke General Hospital, along with Trillium Health Partners' Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital. The province said the initiative responds to emergency departments facing sustained pressure from rising patient volumes, more complex cases and growing demands on the health-care system. EDAT will examine how patients move through emergency departments, from initial assessment and diagnostic testing through to admission or discharge, looking for what's causing delays along the way. The province said the 26 hospitals were chosen based on factors including emergency department volumes and the potential for improvements to benefit the largest number of patients. Insauga reports operational and performance indicators, along with representation across different hospital types and regions, also factored into the selection.

items.title: Mississauga's City Centre Lands Among GTA's Cheapest Neighbourhoods to Buy a Home
items.summary: According to Insauga, real estate platform Wahi's monthly ranking of the Greater Toronto Area's least expensive neighbourhoods placed Mississauga's City Centre among the cheapest places to buy last month, the only Peel Region community on the list. Wahi found City Centre's median sold price was $428,750 in September, with 30 homes selling over an average of about 34 days on the market. Insauga reports North York's Flemington Park topped the overall list with a median price of $383,000, where six homes sold in an average of 26 days, while Etobicoke's Woodbine ranked second at $402,000 with five sales averaging 42 days. Wahi builds its rankings each month using median home sale prices in GTA neighbourhoods with five or more sales. Insauga notes the most expensive neighbourhoods on Wahi's list tended to be older Toronto communities and areas known for large properties, a contrast to the bargains showing up amid the broader market's ongoing slowdown this fall.

items.title: S&P Hands Mississauga Its 23rd Straight Year of Top-Tier AAA Credit Rating
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Standard & Poor's Global Ratings has awarded the city a AAA credit rating, the highest possible, marking the 23rd consecutive year Mississauga has received the designation. The city said the rating reflects strong financial management, responsible budgeting and its ability to stay on solid financial footing while planning for growth and taking on new municipal responsibilities. S&P pointed to Mississauga's careful management of revenues and spending even amid economic uncertainty, along with its ability to fund infrastructure renewal and support housing growth through reserves, responsible debt financing and funding from other levels of government. The ratings agency also highlighted the city's diversified economy, resilient property tax base and strong household incomes as key factors behind its long-term financial stability. S&P noted Mississauga continues to attract business investment despite broader economic and trade-related pressures affecting investment across Canada, particularly in manufacturing, life sciences and technology. The city said its strategic location and transportation network, including Canada's busiest airport, two national railways and five major highways, continue to strengthen its position as a major economic centre.

items.title: Mississauga Turns Park Trails Into Storybook Pages With Year-Round StoryWalk Program
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents can now follow illustrated pages from children's books posted along walking trails at four city parks through the StoryWalk program. Mississauga Library staff chose each book to reflect diverse, family-friendly themes, and every participating park features a different story by a Canadian author, encouraging families to visit multiple locations. The city said the program combines literacy, outdoor recreation and active living, turning a routine walk into an interactive reading adventure for people of all ages. StoryWalk trails are open year-round during regular park hours and are maintained through every season, so residents can take part at their own pace whenever they like. The city invited residents to visit a participating park, get some fresh air and watch a story unfold step by step. Officials noted that once a trail's tale ends, families can continue reading the same stories at Mississauga Library branches.

items.title: 49-Year-Old Mississauga Man Faces 11 Charges After Sarnia Raid Turns Up Loaded Handgun, Drugs
items.summary: According to Insauga, a 49-year-old Mississauga man is facing multiple drug and firearms charges after Sarnia police searched a home in the 1700 block of London Line on Oct. 6 and seized a loaded handgun along with an estimated $16,000 worth of drugs. The Sarnia Police Service Drug Unit carried out the search with help from the force's Intelligence Unit and Emergency Response Team. Officers seized a loaded Taurus 9mm handgun along with additional ammunition during the raid, in addition to the suspected drugs. Police have not released the accused's name, but Insauga reports he faces 11 charges in total, including possession of a prohibited firearm, possession of a firearm while prohibited, possession of ammunition while prohibited, and possession of a firearm without a licence. He is also charged with carrying a concealed weapon, carrying a weapon for a dangerous purpose, and trafficking-related offences involving cocaine and methamphetamine. Police additionally laid a charge of possession of property obtained by crime.
